- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 75+), model tends to overshoot and then overcorrect, failing to capture mean reversion toward lower levels.
- Model underestimates when true price drops sharply from high levels (e.g., 75→70), often by 1–3 points.
- Model shows persistent lag in responding to recent price declines; true price often falls faster than forecast.
- Model tends to overestimate the persistence of recent high prices, underestimating volatility decay.
- Model exhibits bias toward higher prices in the first 10 days of forecast, then gradually adjusts downward — but often too late.
- When true price is below 70, model often fails to recognize the trend and continues to forecast higher values.
- Model underestimates the impact of recent low prices (e.g., 68–70) and fails to trigger a stronger downward correction.
- Model overcorrects after a sharp drop, leading to a false rebound in the middle of the forecast horizon.
- Model does not adequately capture the “mean reversion” effect after prolonged high prices — tends to hold high values longer than observed.
